aidb_assessment.novelty: Moderate to high. The general memory-poisoning phenomenon is acknowledged as prior work, but the paper contributes a clear serializer-level causal account, a nine-harness structural control, executed consequences in the compaction channel, and a paired real-product demonstration.
aidb_assessment.rationale: Adopt the structural mitigation—role-typed serialization or delimiter escaping—and add regression tests now. Treat the post-hoc provenance validator as defense in depth rather than a complete fix. Confidence is high in the existence and mechanism of the flaw, but only medium in precise execution-rate estimates because of small samples and limited end-to-end coverage.
aidb_assessment.usefulness: High for coding-agent implementers and security reviewers. The findings translate directly into design checks: retain typed roles, escape in-band markers, preserve provenance through summaries, keep external approval and sandbox gates, and test compaction with adversarial tool output.

executive_summary: The paper identifies context compaction as a security boundary: serializers that replace typed roles with forgeable text labels can turn attacker-controlled document content into apparent user instructions. Its strongest evidence is a controlled nine-harness comparison, paired clean arms, sandboxed command execution, and a small end-to-end pi TUI study. Flattening harnesses laundered forged approvals while role-typed controls did not; the live attack succeeded in 3/6 poisoned takes versus 0/5 clean takes. The causal mechanism is persuasive, but precise execution rates are uncertain because most execution cells contain only 3–5 runs, released products were usually not exercised end to end, and the defense lacks adaptive evaluation. Serializer escaping or retained typed provenance is more compelling than the partially effective post-hoc validator.

assumptions: The attacker can cause the agent to read attacker-controlled content before compaction.
The affected serializer does not escape role labels appearing inside untrusted content.
For the principal command-execution measurements, the model is effectively the execution gate; an enforced external approval mechanism or OS sandbox can block the demonstrated network command.
A benign canary is an adequate mechanical indicator of attacker-controlled execution, but not of the execution rate for overt credential theft or other high-stakes payloads.
The LLM laundering judge and salience judge adequately represent their stated scoring criteria; only the laundering judge receives a reported cross-family validation sample.
key_components: Threat model with attacker-controlled file, web page, or dependency documentation containing an in-band role marker.
Structural comparison between flattening serializers and role-typed message arrays, with the latter used as controls.
Primary laundering judgment based on whether the summary speaks for the user without preserving the external origin.
Sandboxed downstream agent that can issue a real command and create a host-observed proof artifact.
End-to-end paired pi TUI sessions differing only by one forged line in the fetched guide.
Post-hoc provenance-contrast defense that compares user-attributed summary claims with retained genuine user turns.
method.overview: The authors inspect and pin real compaction prompts and serializers, inject a forged role marker into tool output, compact controlled conversations with frontier models, and score whether the resulting summary attributes the forged claim to the user. They separate laundering from downstream action, compare poisoned, genuine-approval, and clean arms, execute benign payloads in disposable containers, vary model, harness, context size, placement, repetition, and prompt defenses, and run a paired live demonstration in pi.

open_questions: How prevalent are unescaped role-label serializers in proprietary agents and in downstream products derived from the five affected harnesses?
Does delimiter escaping reduce forged-label laundering to an acceptably low level across all harnesses, models, label variants, encodings, and nested document formats?
Can an adaptive attacker evade provenance contrast by matching genuine user vocabulary, paraphrasing prior turns, or splitting authority across multiple fragments?
Do independent salience judges and heterogeneous acting models reproduce the size, recency, and execution relationships?
What harms remain executable when network access, filesystem scope, approval prompts, and process isolation are enforced outside the model?
How do repeated natural compactions, rather than directly invoked synthetic compactions, affect provenance and execution in long-lived real projects?

problem.importance: The corrupted summary can assert standing authorization, steer an agent away from security-relevant files, or contribute to attacker-controlled command execution. The issue affects the ordinary compaction path rather than requiring a separate persistent-memory component.
problem.scope: The study examines nine released harnesses: five flattening systems and four role-typed controls. Most experiments exercise pinned serializers and compaction prompts in a staged runner; one experiment exercises the real pi TUI end to end. Execution measurements primarily cover model-only or full-auto conditions and benign canary payloads.
problem.statement: Long-running coding agents replace an original typed conversation with a compact summary. If the harness first flattens roles into unescaped in-band labels, attacker-controlled files or pages can forge a user turn whose true source disappears when the original transcript is discarded.

proposed_experiments.baseline: Unpatched serializer, plain-text payload without a forged label, and role-typed serializer control, evaluated on the same harness-model-transcript matrix.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Escaping every in-band role marker before flattening reduces forged-label laundering to the plain-text level without materially harming legitimate-summary fidelity.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: Difference in laundering rate between patched forged-label and plain-text arms, with legitimate-summary retention as a co-primary safety metric.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop when confidence intervals are narrow enough to exclude a practically important excess over the plain-text arm, or when any patched harness shows a reproducible laundering pathway requiring redesign.

proposed_experiments.baseline: The published generic payload suite at the recommended provenance-contrast setting, plus clean summaries for collateral measurement.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: An adaptive attacker can reduce the provenance-contrast defense’s catch rate by matching the vocabulary and paraphrase style of genuine user turns.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: Adaptive laundering escape rate at a fixed legitimate-claim demotion budget.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop after the adaptive attack reaches a stable plateau across held-out users and models, or immediately if escape becomes high enough that the defense no longer improves materially over the prompt baseline.

proposed_experiments.baseline: The original single-model baseline, recency, repetition, and framing conditions at matched context sizes.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: The reported salience-execution association generalizes when summary generation, salience judgment, and downstream action use different model families.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: Command-issuance rate stratified by independently judged salience, with effect sizes and uncertainty across summarizer–judge–executor combinations.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop when the direction of the salience effect is replicated across multiple independent combinations with adequate precision, or when the association reverses or disappears in enough combinations to reject generality.

artifacts: Public repository containing experiment harnesses and runners.
Pinned upstream prompts, serializers, sources, and commits for all nine harnesses.
Containerized live demonstration with operator script, paired takes, recordings, session logs, and per-take digests.
Scoring code and an independent adjudication record for the laundering judge.
reproducibility.assessment: Reproducibility is strong for an empirical security paper because the authors report pinned upstream components, runnable code, raw table data, containment infrastructure, scoring code, recordings, and paired live artifacts. The strongest remaining gaps concern external validity and unperformed experiments rather than absence of the reported artifacts.
missing: A reported independent multi-model replication of the salience mechanism.
Adaptive-attack evaluation for the provenance-contrast defense.
End-to-end product runs for harnesses other than pi.
Large-sample execution estimates and broader non-GPT execution coverage.
A larger clean corpus for estimating defense collateral.
Executed tests of recombination attacks and harms under enforced OS sandboxes.

results.context: Each harness used its real serializer and compaction prompt on three frontier models. This is the strongest controlled evidence for the structural serialization hypothesis, although the outcome is laundering rather than live execution.

evidence.quote: We planted the identical forged approval in nine released harnesses and ran each one’s real serializer and real compaction prompt on three frontier models (n = 15 per harness).
Flattening pi, opencode, Aider 100% (15/15) Flattening OpenHands 93% (14/15) Flattening Cline 87% (13/15)
Role-typed Codex, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, Continue 0% (0/15)

results.result: In the main cross-harness comparison, pi, opencode, and Aider laundered 100% (15/15), OpenHands 93% (14/15), and Cline 87% (13/15), whereas Codex, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, and Continue produced 0% (0/15).

results.context: This paired end-to-end experiment is the most operationally relevant evidence, but its sample is small and uses one harness and one victim model.

evidence.quote: arm full chain (WIN) refused post-compaction ran pre-compaction (attack unnecessary) poisoned 3/6 3/6 0/6 clean 0/5 5/5 1/6 †
†one clean take executed the bootstrap during its first turn, before any compaction — model variance, not the attack — and the paired design absorbs it.

results.result: The real pi TUI produced a full-chain win in 3/6 poisoned takes and 0/5 clean takes; all poisoned takes refused pre-compaction execution, while one clean take executed before compaction and was excluded from the attack’s causal sequence.

results.context: The comparison favors checking summary attribution in code, but the classifier figures are imported from prior work rather than re-measured on the same implementation, and the defense was not tested against adaptive payloads.

evidence.quote: Gemini’s in-prompt rule stops ~13% of laundering on Claude, ~25% on GPT
Published classifier defenses [2] 67% catch rate at best, 42% on low-signal payloads

results.result: At the recommended provenance-contrast setting of 0.15, the defense caught 77% of laundering while demoting 2% of legitimate claims. The compared prompt rule stopped about 13% on Claude and 25% on GPT, while the cited classifier baseline reached 67% at best and 42% on low-signal payloads.

results.context: This consequential negative result limits the broad RCE interpretation and supports the paper’s separation between false authorization and artifact verification. The audit was scripted and deliberately strong.

evidence.quote: execution collapses to 1/50 pooled across all arms and both models.
1/50 with the maximal forgery, versus E15’s ~50% when the audit is absent.

results.result: A genuine skeptical audit sharply reduced downstream execution: pooled across all E16 arms and both models, execution was 1/50 even though forged user approval still laundered reliably. This contrasts with the live study’s approximately 50% success when the audit disappeared during compaction.
